newsitem.title: FRANCE: France faults Israel on Jerusalem tunnel.
newsitem.headline: France faults Israel on Jerusalem tunnel.

text.p: France accused Israel on Wednesday of fuelling Middle East tension by opening a disputed archeological tunnel beneath the Old City of Jerusalem.

As Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived in Paris for talks with President Jacques Chirac, French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said: "The opening of a tunnel by the Israelis under the (Temple Mount) mosques esplanade and the Arab city of Jerusalem is an old project that had been frozen for 10 years. This initiatve adds a new and regrettable factor of tension."

In Jerusalem, Israeli police fired rubber bullets and teargas to disperse stone-throwing students demonstrating against Israel's opening of the tourist tunnel beneath the Wailing Wall, sacred to Jews, and near al-Aqsa mosque, one of Islam's holiest shrine.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called a general strike in the Israeli-occupied territories, calling the tunnel a crime against the Moslem religion and the Arab-Israeli peace process.
Netanyahu defended the opening of the tunnel on Tuesday, telling reporters on his plane: "(It is) a decision I am very proud that we are implementing".

French officials said Chirac would tell Netanyahu over lunch that Paris wanted him to move forward with the peace process initiated by his Labour predecessors and was ready to help in negotiations with Syria and Lebanon.
